title: Recovery and trying his horn again at the Wollman Rink
summary: After four or five months of rest he readjusted, practised at Pleasantville, and went to hear Duke at Wollman Rink where Duke invited him to play the next show.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: So your blood pressure, and you stopped. But then you went back to the band.

Oh, I had a complete rest. I think it was about 4 months, 5 months, something like that. Then again, which was a third phase in my life that I had to readjust. I had two phases before that and this was the third. So -- and you don't know how a man -- and you can lay in the bed in the hospital and think. Oh, I'm telling you. You count all the bricks in the building. You count all the spokes in the bed. You count all the footsteps that you hear out in the hallway, and so on. But then I realized that I had to stop doing a lot of things I had been doing and start doing a lot of things, you know, vice-versa. So I

-- and then, as I say, it's a complete adjustment, because you don't know how you'll feel when you come out of the hospital and come back home. It's a new thing, believe me. You're scared to cross the street. You see the traffic coming. You know, you're just like a little child. That sort of thing. So anyway, I adjusted and I got back.
I remember Duke was playing -- what's the name of the place over in Central Park? The Wellmann --

Yeah. So he was playing there, so I went over there one day. I think I was just starting getting back, getting my horn, you know, getting my fingers to working, and I had been down to Pleasantville, New Jersey. You know, we have a place down there, you know, sort of a summer home, I guess you'd call it, and I'd been spending time down there. And I remember I went to Atlantic City and brought some reeds, when I decided to start blowing again. So I went by this Memorial, and Duke was playing there. He had an afternoon concert and a night concert. So I went to hear the band and I went backstage after the afternoon performance, and I had my horn with me, so Duke said, 'Well, come on, play this next show.' I said, 'Oh, no. No, no. I'm not ready.'
